proposals.before: During the Dazhun era he rose to commander of cavalry and infantry and, together with Li Cunxiao, attacked Zhang Jun's forces at Pingyang.
proposals.after: During the Dashun era he rose to commander of cavalry and infantry and, together with Li Cunxiao, attacked Zhang Jun's forces at Pingyang.
proposals.reason: 大順 is Dashun (AD 890-891), not Dazhun; the English reign name is a mistransliteration.

proposals.before: In the Dazhun era he was repeatedly promoted to commander of horse and foot, and with Li Cunxiao struck Zhang Jun's army at Pingyang.
proposals.after: In the Dashun era he was repeatedly promoted to commander of horse and foot, and with Li Cunxiao struck Zhang Jun's army at Pingyang.
proposals.reason: 大順 is Dashun, not Dazhun; the literal English repeats the same reign-name error.

proposals.before: In the second year of Dazhun the Martial Emperor launched a major campaign east of the mountains and appointed Cunxin commander of barbarian and Han horse and foot. Cunxiao flew into a rage. The Martial Emperor sent Cunzhi to take the post in his place, whereupon Cunxiao began plotting rebellion.
proposals.after: In the second year of Dashun the Martial Emperor launched a major campaign east of the mountains and appointed Cunxin commander of barbarian and Han horse and foot. Cunxiao flew into a rage. The Martial Emperor sent Cunzhi to take the post in his place, whereupon Cunxiao began plotting rebellion.
proposals.reason: 大順二年 is Dashun 2 (AD 891). Dazhun is a mistransliteration of the reign name.

proposals.before: In the second year of Dazhun the Martial Emperor made a great expedition to seize territory in Shandong, appointing Cunxin as commander of barbarian and Han horse and foot; when Cunxiao heard of it he was angry; the Martial Emperor had Cunzhi replace him, and Cunxiao then plotted rebellion.
proposals.after: In the second year of Dashun the Martial Emperor made a great expedition to seize territory in Shandong, appointing Cunxin as commander of barbarian and Han horse and foot; when Cunxiao heard of it he was angry; the Martial Emperor had Cunzhi replace him, and Cunxiao then plotted rebellion.
proposals.reason: 大順二年 is Dashun 2; the literal English inherits the same Dazhun error.

proposals.before: In the third year of Qianning, Yan and Yun sought reinforcements from the Martial Emperor. He sent Cunxin to encamp at Shen County and unite with Zhu Xuan against Liang.
proposals.after: In the third year of Qianning, Yan and Yun sought reinforcements from the Martial Emperor. He sent Cunxin to encamp at Xin County and unite with Zhu Xuan against Liang.
proposals.reason: 莘縣 is Xin County (modern Shenxian/莘县, historically Xīn), not Shen County.

proposals.before: In the third year of Qianning, Yan and Yun requested troops from the Martial Emperor; he sent Cunxin to encamp at Shen County and join forces with Zhu Xuan to resist the men of Liang.
proposals.after: In the third year of Qianning, Yan and Yun requested troops from the Martial Emperor; he sent Cunxin to encamp at Xin County and join forces with Zhu Xuan to resist the men of Liang.
proposals.reason: 莘縣 should be Xin County; Shen is a wrong reading of 莘.

proposals.before: Cunxin drew his troops back but was worsted by the Wei forces, abandoned his baggage, and fell back to Ming Prefecture, losing perhaps a fifth of his army.
proposals.after: Cunxin drew his troops back but was worsted by the Wei forces, abandoned his baggage, and fell back to Ming Prefecture, losing two or three tenths of his army.
proposals.reason: 十二三 means two or three out of ten (20–30 percent), not 'a fifth'.

proposals.before: When Zhang Jun marched additional forces against Taiyuan, a Luzhou junior officer named Feng Ba killed his commander Li Keong and turned the city in revolt.
proposals.after: When Zhang Jun marched additional forces against Taiyuan, a Luzhou junior officer named Feng Ba killed his commander Li Kegong and turned the city in revolt.
proposals.reason: 李克恭 is Li Kegong; Keong drops the g of 恭 (gong).

proposals.before: When Zhang Jun added troops against Taiyuan, a minor officer of Luzhou, Feng Ba, killed his commander Li Keong and rebelled with the city.
proposals.after: When Zhang Jun added troops against Taiyuan, a minor officer of Luzhou, Feng Ba, killed his commander Li Kegong and rebelled with the city.
proposals.reason: 李克恭 should be Li Kegong, not Li Keong.

proposals.before: That night the Bian general Li Dan broke camp and fled. Cunxiao pursued to Malaoshan, taking and killing enemies by the tens of thousands, then turned back to invest Luzhou.
proposals.after: That night the Bian general Li Dang broke camp and fled. Cunxiao pursued to Malaoshan, taking and killing enemies by the tens of thousands, then turned back to invest Luzhou.
proposals.reason: 李讜 is Li Dang (Dǎng); Dan is the wrong reading of 讜.

proposals.before: That night the Bian general Li Dan gathered his army and fled; Cunxiao pursued to Malaoshan, capturing and slaying tens of thousands, then withdrew to attack Luzhou.
proposals.after: That night the Bian general Li Dang gathered his army and fled; Cunxiao pursued to Malaoshan, capturing and slaying tens of thousands, then withdrew to attack Luzhou.
proposals.reason: 李讜 should be romanized Li Dang, not Li Dan.

proposals.before: In the third month of the second year of Dazhun, Xingzhou commissioner An Zhijian defected to the Bian army. The Martial Emperor sent Cunxiao to secure Xing and Ming and invested him with the commissioner's regalia.
proposals.after: In the third month of the second year of Dashun, Xingzhou commissioner An Zhijian defected to the Bian army. The Martial Emperor sent Cunxiao to secure Xing and Ming and invested him with the commissioner's regalia.
proposals.reason: 大順二年 is Dashun 2 (AD 891). Dazhun is a mistransliteration.

proposals.before: In the third month of the second year of Dazhun, An Zhijian, military commissioner of Xing Prefecture, rebelled and entered the Bian army; the Martial Emperor ordered Cunxiao to pacify Xing and Ming and thereby invested him with commission and regalia.
proposals.after: In the third month of the second year of Dashun, An Zhijian, military commissioner of Xing Prefecture, rebelled and entered the Bian army; the Martial Emperor ordered Cunxiao to pacify Xing and Ming and thereby invested him with commission and regalia.
proposals.reason: 大順二年 is Dashun 2, not Dazhun.

proposals.before: In the third month of the first year of Qianning Cunxiao mounted the wall to confess his guilt and wept before the Martial Emperor: "I owed you deep kindness and rose to command armies. Had slanderers not driven us apart, why would I ever have forsaken a father's bond to join your enemies?!
proposals.after: In the third month of the first year of Qianning, Cunxiao mounted the wall to confess his guilt and wept before the Martial Emperor: "I owed you deep kindness and rose to command armies. Had slanderers not driven us apart, why would I ever have forsaken a father's bond to join your enemies?!
proposals.reason: A comma is required after Qianning so the reign name is not fused with the personal name Cunxiao.

proposals.before: In the ninth month Wang Chuqiong marched out with his full strength, caught them unprepared, and burst upon the rampart gate.
proposals.after: In the ninth month Wang Chuqiu marched out with his full strength, caught them unprepared, and burst upon the rampart gate.
proposals.reason: 王處球 is Wang Chuqiu (球 qiú); Chuqiong would be 瓊.

proposals.before: In the ninth month Wang Chuqiong led out all his forces, taking advantage of their unreadiness, and suddenly reached the rampart gate.
proposals.after: In the ninth month Wang Chuqiu led out all his forces, taking advantage of their unreadiness, and suddenly reached the rampart gate.
proposals.reason: 王處球 should be romanized Wang Chuqiu, not Wang Chuqiong.

proposals.before: Zhixiang said, "Old companions from Fen and Pei meeting again here—what could bring greater joy!"
proposals.after: Zhixiang said, "Old companions from Feng and Pei meeting again here—what could bring greater joy!"
proposals.reason: 豐沛 is Feng and Pei (the Han-founder allusion), not Fen; Fen is 汾 from the previous sentence.

proposals.before: In the eleventh year he was made prefect of Wu and training commissioner of Shannan.
proposals.after: In the eleventh year he was made prefect of Wu and training commissioner of Shanbei.
proposals.reason: 山北團練使 is the training commissioner north of the mountains (Shanbei), not Shannan (山南).

proposals.before: In the eleventh year he was appointed prefect of Wu and training commissioner of Shannan.
proposals.after: In the eleventh year he was appointed prefect of Wu and training commissioner of Shanbei.
proposals.reason: 山北 is Shanbei, not Shannan.
